paragraph_functions: context: Wordle popularity and simple rules
Task-1: Gaussian regression + Poisson + popularity relaxation, CI [7654,20154], 8 attributes null on hard mode
Task-2: BP NN + Bagging, EERIE distribution, 80% confidence within 5%
Task-3: K-Means 4 classes + Pearson correlation, EERIR as Master
Task-4: distribution pattern similar to trend, 3-tries fluctuation largest
closing: sensitivity analysis + keywords
hook: Homer as Cambridge Dictionary 2022 Word of Year via Wordle
game-rules: color-coded feedback explanation
restatement: 4 bulleted problem requirements
lit-review-1: Shen RPP, Zhao SEISMIC, Wu EPAB
lit-review-2: limitations of existing approaches
our-contribution: extract all info from Data File
paper-structure: Figure 1 flowchart
organization: section-by-section roadmap
game-rules-detail: color tile meanings
motivation: mine Wordle report information

opening: Homer anecdote hook with Cambridge Dictionary

paragraph_functions: intro: general assumptions to simplify
assumption-1: reported users reflect actual player changes
assumption-2: one play per person per day, reset at 0:00 EST
assumption-3: players have literacy and problem-solving skills
assumption-4: historical data represents all possible questions
notation-table: Table 1 with 5 symbol definitions
check: word length anomalies (4 or 6 letters)
correction: No.529 outlier corrected by averaging
task-1-intro: explore variation pattern, statistical perspective
data-exploration: dynamic pattern over time, trend + fluctuation
fluctuation-popularity: correlation between fluctuation and game heat
goal: build mathematical model for description and prediction
gap: two classes of algorithms inapplicable + two reasons
gaussian-intro: 3rd-order Gaussian regression for trend
gaussian-equation: regression equation (1) with coefficients
loss-function: least squares (2)
poisson-intro: non-homogeneous Poisson for random fluctuation
poisson-equation: arrival intensity (3)
mean-approximation: use Gaussian result as mean function
lifecycle: Explosion, Fading, Dormant periods by analogy
relaxation-function: linear boundary popularity relaxation
modified-intensity: corrected arrival intensity (4)
corrected-probability: modified equation (5)
prediction-interval: confidence-based interval (6)
regression-results: R2=0.9988, RMSE 2 orders smaller
Table-2: regression coefficients
interval-result: 75% CI [7654, 20154], convergence 13904
game-mode-intro: 8 word attributes
attribute-1-to-8: detailed definitions with happy examples
scatter-analysis: no strong correlation with hard mode
Table-4: top/bottom 10 hard mode percentages
time-trend: hard mode increases over time, then levels off
interpretation: confidence and mentality as main reasons
ambiguities: Section 5.3 game mode selection within model-establishment.

paragraph_functions: task-2-intro: predict distribution using features + BP NN
data-limitation: mechanistic modeling infeasible
feature-extraction: 7 features from words and time
feature-pruning: remove common root (unbalanced) and total letters (redundant)
hard-mode-feature: predictable from time trend
bp-architecture: 3-layer, 7-7-7, hidden layer via empirical formula (7)
bagging: integrated BP via random 85% subsampling
voting: hard voting mechanism for final prediction
uncertainty: dataset representativeness, sub-training homogeneity
results: RMSE, correlation 0.84, error distribution, EERIE prediction
task-3-intro: classify words by difficulty
difficulty-definition: user guess distribution, not word attributes
k-means-euclidean: equation (8) Euclidean distance
centers: determine K by multiple attempts
algorithm: iterative centroid + sample allocation (9)
convergence: objective function comparison
pearson-intro: correlation between attributes and difficulty
attribute-selection: 7 attributes including WCN and VN
correlation-results: Table 6, F2=0.81, VN=0.90, WCN=0.82
euclidean-classification: two methods (distribution-based + attribute-based)
EERIR-result: Master (R4=0.625 closest to Dandy)
word-cloud: Figure 13 visualization

transition: From a mathematical point of view

paragraph_functions: design: fine-tune popularity relaxation intercept
conclusion: somewhat robust, not for large fluctuations
strengths: decomposition interpretability + user-experience difficulty + Bagging generalization
weaknesses: wide CI in popular phases + dataset representativeness
further: social network analysis + sentiment integration
summary-intro: propose series of novel models
conclusion-1: report number model combines trend + fluctuation
conclusion-2: hard mode not affected by word attributes
conclusion-3: distribution model combines word + time features
conclusion-4: difficulty classification combines distribution + attributes
letter-opening: happy to dig into mystery, social currency metaphor
letter-models: three models described for editor
letter-findings: valuable findings for puzzle development
letter-results: interval, distribution, difficulty predictions
letter-closing: thanks for busy schedule, hope can help

units.source_excerpt: Wordle is a popular puzzle currently offered daily by the New York Times. The simple rules and clever propagation properties have contributed to its popularity.
units.reusable_pattern: [Subject] is a popular [category] currently offered by [institution]. [Properties] have contributed to its popularity
reusable_elements: [Subject] is a popular [category] currently offered by [institution]. [Properties] have contributed to its popularity.
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid attributing popularity without evidence

units.source_excerpt: In this article, we build two prediction models for the prediction of the Twitter report number intervals and result distributions, respectively, and develop a model for classifying the difficulty of solution words.
units.reusable_pattern: In this article, we build [N] prediction models for [target-A] and [target-B], respectively, and develop a model for [target-C]
reusable_elements: In this article, we build [N] prediction models for [target-A] and [target-B], and develop a model for [target-C]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'respectively' when targets are not parallel

units.source_excerpt: In TASK 1: After data preprocessing, we build a Wordle report number prediction model based on 3rd-order gaussian regression and a non-homogeneous Poisson process from a statistical perspective.
units.reusable_pattern: In TASK [N]: After [preprocessing], we build [model] based on [technique-A] and [technique-B] from a [perspective] perspective
reusable_elements: In TASK [N]: After [step], we build [model] based on [technique-A] and [technique-B] from a [perspective] perspective
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'from a statistical perspective' as padding

units.source_excerpt: Moreover, we use the popularity relaxation function to correct the stochastic process, which better approximates the popularity change.
units.reusable_pattern: Moreover, we use [function] to correct [process], which better approximates [target]
reusable_elements: Moreover, we use [function] to correct [process], which better approximates [target]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim 'better' without baseline comparison

units.source_excerpt: At a confidence level of 75%, we predict the interval of the number of reports on March 1, 2023 to be [7654, 20154].
units.reusable_pattern: At a confidence level of [X]%, we predict [target] to be [interval]
reusable_elements: At a confidence level of [X]%, we predict [target] to be [interval]
prohibited_generalizations: State why 75% rather than 95% was chosen

units.source_excerpt: In addition, we extract 8 attributes of words in terms of the number of letters, letter location and so on, finding that these attributes did not have an effect on the percentage of players' Hard Mode choices.
units.reusable_pattern: In addition, we extract [N] attributes of [category] in terms of [list], finding that [null-result]
reusable_elements: In addition, we extract [N] attributes of [items] in terms of [list], finding that [null-result]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'and so on' — enumerate or omit

units.source_excerpt: Players' confidence in their performance ability and their play mentality may be the main reasons for whether they choose the Hard Mode or not.
units.reusable_pattern: [Factor-A] and [Factor-B] may be the main reasons for [outcome]
reusable_elements: [Factor-A] and [Factor-B] may be the main reasons for [behavioral-outcome]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim psychological factors without measurement

units.source_excerpt: In TASK 2: We first extract the data features that affect the distribution of reported results, including word attributes, and the percentage of difficulty patterns. Then, we build a BP neural network to make preliminary predictions.
units.reusable_pattern: In TASK [N]: We first extract [features]. Then, we build [model] to [goal]
reusable_elements: In TASK [N]: We first extract [features]. Then, we build [model] to [goal]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'preliminary predictions' — state confidence level

units.source_excerpt: To improve the generalization performance of the prediction results, we build an integrated BP neural network based on Bagging.
units.reusable_pattern: To improve [quality], we build [integrated-model] based on [algorithm]
reusable_elements: To improve [quality] of [results], we build [integrated model] based on [algorithm]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim generalization improvement without test-set evidence

units.source_excerpt: We have more than 80% confidence that the absolute error of the predicted outcome for the percentage of each possible result does not exceed 5%.
units.reusable_pattern: We have more than [X]% confidence that [error-metric] does not exceed [threshold]
reusable_elements: We have more than [X]% confidence that [metric] does not exceed [threshold]
prohibited_generalizations: Specify whether confidence is frequentist or empirical

units.source_excerpt: In TASK 3: First, we build a word difficulty induction model based on the K-Means from the distribution of user's reported data, and divide the difficulty into 4 classes.
units.reusable_pattern: In TASK [N]: First, we build [model] based on [algorithm] from [data], and divide [target] into [N] classes
reusable_elements: In TASK [N]: First, we build [model] based on [algorithm] from [data], and divide [target] into [N] classes
prohibited_generalizations: State why K classes instead of K-1 or K+1

units.source_excerpt: Moreover, we find that the frequency of the first and second letters of the solution words, the number of vowels contained in the pronunciation and the number of word properties have a high correlation with the difficulty classification.
units.reusable_pattern: Moreover, we find that [attribute-list] have a high correlation with [target]
reusable_elements: Moreover, we find that [attributes] have a high correlation with [classification]
prohibited_generalizations: Specify correlation coefficient, not just 'high'

units.source_excerpt: Finally, the difficulty classification result of EERIR is the most difficult.
units.reusable_pattern: Finally, the [classification] result of [example] is [label]
reusable_elements: Finally, the [classification] result of [example] is [label]
prohibited_generalizations: State label name, not relative descriptor

units.source_excerpt: In TASK 4: While exploring the statistical properties of the number of reports, we find that the distribution of the number of reports showed a similar pattern to its trend over time.
units.reusable_pattern: In TASK [N]: While exploring [properties], we find that [distribution] showed a similar pattern to [trend]
reusable_elements: In TASK [N]: While exploring [properties], we find that [observation]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'similar pattern' without quantifying similarity

units.source_excerpt: Keywords: Gaussian regression; Poisson process; BP neural network; K-Means
units.reusable_pattern: Keywords: [semicolon-separated list]
reusable_elements: Keywords: [Technique-1]; [Technique-2]; [Technique-3]; [Technique-4]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list generic algorithms as keywords

units.source_excerpt: Homer is a term used in the sport of baseball and is an informal American English word. Amazingly, Homer (home run) was searched over 79,000 times on the Cambridge Dictionary website.
units.reusable_pattern: [Term] is a [category]. Amazingly, [term] was [action] over [N] times on [platform]
reusable_elements: [Term] is a [category]. Amazingly, [term] was [action] over [N] times on [platform]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'Amazingly' as filler — let data speak

units.source_excerpt: You may be wondering why, but it starts with Wordle, a very popular word-guessing game overseas.
units.reusable_pattern: You may be wondering why, but it starts with [subject], a [description]
reusable_elements: You may be wondering why, but it starts with [subject], a [description]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid second-person address in academic writing

units.source_excerpt: Shen et al first established a Reinforced Poisson Processes (RPP) model to predict dynamic prevalence using a heterogeneous Poisson process model, and considered the 'rich get richer'.
units.reusable_pattern: [Author] et al first established [model] to [goal] using [method], and considered [phenomenon]
reusable_elements: [Author] et al first established [model] to [goal] using [method], and considered [phenomenon]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid multiple citations in one sentence without distinguishing contributions

units.source_excerpt: However, the time series model requires the data set to contain timing information, and the data set that does not meet this condition cannot be modeled.
units.reusable_pattern: However, [existing-approach] requires [condition], and [data] that does not meet this cannot be [action]
reusable_elements: However, [approach] requires [condition], and [data] that does not meet this cannot be [action]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss approaches without trying them

units.source_excerpt: In this paper, we try our best to extract all the information from the Data File. Aiming at the specific application scenario of Wordle, we not only realize the interval prediction but also carry out further analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: In this paper, we try our best to [goal]. Aiming at [scenario], we not only [A] but also [B]
reusable_elements: In this paper, we [goal]. Aiming at [scenario], we not only [A] but also [B]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'try our best' — state what was achieved

units.source_excerpt: We put forward three models to mine the information of the reported result data. The structure of our paper is shown in Figure 1.
units.reusable_pattern: We put forward [N] models to [goal]. The structure of our paper is shown in Figure [N]
reusable_elements: We put forward [N] models to [goal]. The structure of our paper is shown in Figure [N]
prohibited_generalizations: Use 'propose' instead of 'put forward'

units.source_excerpt: The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section II, we introduce the premise assumptions and justifications, and common variables in the formulas are mentioned in Section III.
units.reusable_pattern: The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section [N], we [content]. [Section] [content]
reusable_elements: The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section [N], we [content].
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid listing every section — only highlight non-obvious structure

units.source_excerpt: We make some general assumptions to simplify our model. These assumptions together with corresponding justifications are listed below.
units.reusable_pattern: We make some general assumptions to simplify our model. These assumptions with justifications are listed below
reusable_elements: We make some general assumptions to simplify our model. These assumptions with justifications are listed below.
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'some general' — be specific about count

units.source_excerpt: It is assumed that the change in the number of users in the report is a true reflection of the change in players in the actual situation. There may be players who are enthusiastic but do not tweet their results.
units.reusable_pattern: It is assumed that [claim]. [Counterpoint], however [justification]
reusable_elements: It is assumed that [claim]. [Counterpoint], however [justification]
prohibited_generalizations: Acknowledge selection bias rather than assuming representativeness

units.source_excerpt: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table 1.
units.reusable_pattern: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table [N]
reusable_elements: The key mathematical notations used in this paper are listed in Table [N].
prohibited_generalizations: Define symbols inline at first use, not only in tables

units.source_excerpt: Before building the model, a preliminary check of the data in the report is needed. According to the rules of Wordle, each word is 5 letters long. But there are unusual statistics of 4 or 6 letters in the data.
units.reusable_pattern: Before building [model], a preliminary check is needed. According to [rules], [expected]. But [anomaly] in [data]
reusable_elements: Before building [model], a preliminary check is needed. According to [rules], [expected]. But [anomaly] in [data]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'preliminary check' — state what was checked

units.source_excerpt: To explore the variation pattern of the number of reported results obtained from Twitter over time, we first develop an interpretable model for describing and predicting the number of reports.
units.reusable_pattern: To explore [pattern] over time, we first develop an interpretable model for [goal]
reusable_elements: To explore [pattern] over time, we first develop an interpretable model for [goal]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'interpretable' without defining interpretability criteria

units.source_excerpt: In general, there is a certain pattern of popularity propagation law in the number of reports on the time scale. When Wordle exploded in the early days, there was a significant increase; however, when the popularity period passed, the number showed a downward trend and leveled off.
units.reusable_pattern: In general, there is a [pattern] in [data]. When [event-A], [increase]; however, when [event-B], [decrease] and leveled off
reusable_elements: In general, there is a [pattern] in [data]. When [event-A], [increase]; however, when [event-B], [decrease] and leveled off.
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'a certain pattern' — describe the pattern

units.source_excerpt: In other words, the process of the number of reports over time can be divided into two parts, which are trend signs and random fluctuation.
units.reusable_pattern: In other words, [process] can be divided into [N] parts: [part-A] and [part-B]
reusable_elements: In other words, [process] can be divided into [N] parts: [part-A] and [part-B]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'In other words' restating — consolidate

units.source_excerpt: We want to build a mathematical model based on existing data to describe the process of changing the number of reported results on Twitter over time and to predict the popularity in a certain period in the future, and the model is explanatory for the change process.
units.reusable_pattern: We want to build a mathematical model based on [data] to describe [process] and predict [target], and the model is explanatory
reusable_elements: We want to build a mathematical model based on [data] to describe [process] and predict [target], and the model is explanatory.
prohibited_generalizations: Use 'aim to build' instead of 'want to build'

units.source_excerpt: By reviewing the literature, we learned that two classes of heat prediction algorithms are commonly used in the industry. However, they do not apply to the scenario studied in this paper. This is mainly due to the following two reasons.
units.reusable_pattern: By reviewing literature, we learned [N] classes [exist]. However, they do not apply to [scenario]. This is due to [N] reasons
reusable_elements: By reviewing literature, we learned [methods exist]. However, they do not apply. This is due to [N] reasons:
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss all existing methods without empirical comparison

units.source_excerpt: We tried several regression algorithms to fit the trend in the number of reports over time, and the best result was a 3rd order Gaussian regression.
units.reusable_pattern: We tried several [algorithms] to fit [target], and the best result was [chosen-method]
reusable_elements: We tried several [algorithms] to fit [target], and the best result was [chosen-method]
prohibited_generalizations: Report all alternatives tried, not just winner

units.source_excerpt: The Poisson distribution describes the probability of a certain number of events occurring over a period of time under the condition that the event occurrence rate is constant, and thus can describe the probability of a certain number of reports uploaded in a day.
units.reusable_pattern: [Distribution] describes the probability of [events] under [condition], and thus can describe [application]
reusable_elements: [Distribution] describes the probability of [events] under [condition], and thus can describe [application]
prohibited_generalizations: Separate textbook definition from application

units.source_excerpt: By analogy with the life cycle of online public opinion, this paper divides the life cycle of Wordle's popularity trend: i. Explosion Period, ii. Fading Period, iii. Dormant Period.
units.reusable_pattern: By analogy with [reference], this paper divides [subject] into [N] periods: [list]
reusable_elements: By analogy with [reference], this paper divides [subject] into [N] periods: [list]
prohibited_generalizations: Justify lifecycle analogy with evidence from data

units.source_excerpt: We predict that the number of reported results converges to 13,904 on March 1, 2023. The results of the prediction intervals at different confidence levels are shown in Table 3.
units.reusable_pattern: We predict that [quantity] converges to [value] on [date]. Intervals at different confidence levels shown in Table [N]
reusable_elements: We predict that [quantity] converges to [value] on [date]. Intervals shown in Table [N]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use 'converges' for point estimate of random variable

units.source_excerpt: It can be noticed that the individual attributes do not have a strong correlation with the percentage of Hard Mode. The presented word attributes do not affect the proportion of reported data for the Hard Mode.
units.reusable_pattern: It can be noticed that [attributes] do not have strong correlation with [DV]. [Attributes] do not affect [proportion]
reusable_elements: It can be noticed that [attributes] do not have strong correlation with [DV]. [Attributes] do not affect [proportion].
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'it can be noticed' — state directly

units.source_excerpt: We believe that, on the one hand, this is because as the time spent playing the game increases, the user's ability is also sufficiently improved. On the other hand, many users may play with a more casual mindset.
units.reusable_pattern: We believe that, on the one hand, [reason-A]. On the other hand, [reason-B]
reusable_elements: We believe that, on the one hand, [reason-A]. On the other hand, [reason-B]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'We believe' — provide evidence

units.source_excerpt: To predict the distribution of future report results, we first extracted and constructed the data features. Then, we build a BP neural network model to take 7 data features as input and output the distribution of 7 guessed word results.
units.reusable_pattern: To predict [target], we first [extracted features]. Then, we build [model] to take [N] features as input and output [target]
reusable_elements: To predict [target], we first [extract features]. Then, we build [model] to take [N] features as input and output [N-dim result]
prohibited_generalizations: Specify feature count in both input and output

units.source_excerpt: Considering that the result distribution of the number of word guesses shared on Twitter is likely to be different from that of the entire player population, and is related to many factors that are difficult to quantify, mechanistic modeling may be difficult and unrealistic, and we decided to model the data.
units.reusable_pattern: Considering that [data-limitation] and [complexity], mechanistic modeling may be [infeasible], and we decided to [approach]
reusable_elements: Considering that [data limitation] and [complexity], mechanistic modeling may be [infeasible], and we decided to [approach]
prohibited_generalizations: Do not dismiss mechanistic modeling without attempting it

units.source_excerpt: A review of the literature shows that for fitting such finite-dimensional space mappings, building neural networks usually requires only one hidden layer.
units.reusable_pattern: A review of the literature shows that for [task], [architecture] usually requires only [configuration]
reusable_elements: A review of the literature shows that for [task], [architecture] usually requires only [configuration]
prohibited_generalizations: Cite the specific result, not vague 'literature shows'

units.source_excerpt: After several tests, we found that the neural network obtained from each training always has unacceptable errors at very few samples in the test set. Moreover, the repetition rate of samples with large prediction errors was not high for different neural networks. Therefore, we decided to adopt the Bagging algorithm.
units.reusable_pattern: After several tests, we found [problem] at [subset]. Moreover, [low-overlap]. Therefore, we decided to adopt [algorithm]
reusable_elements: After several tests, we found [problem]. Moreover, [observation]. Therefore, we decided to adopt [algorithm]
prohibited_generalizations: Quantify 'unacceptable errors' and 'several tests'

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, we have more than 80% confidence that the absolute error of the prediction result does not exceed 5%.
units.reusable_pattern: Therefore, we have more than [X]% confidence that [error] does not exceed [threshold]
reusable_elements: Therefore, we have more than [X]% confidence that [metric] does not exceed [threshold]
prohibited_generalizations: Distinguish empirical coverage from statistical confidence

units.source_excerpt: To classify the solution words reasonably, we first classified the difficulty based on the K-Means clustering algorithm. Then, we explored the association between word attributes and difficulty based on Pearson correlation coefficients.
units.reusable_pattern: To [goal] reasonably, we first [step-A] based on [algorithm-A]. Then, we [step-B] based on [algorithm-B]
reusable_elements: To [goal], we first [step-A] based on [algorithm-A]. Then, we [step-B] based on [algorithm-B]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'reasonably' — let method justify itself

units.source_excerpt: To make the model result more similar to the user's game experience, we decided to define a difficulty division based on the user's guess count distribution. It should be noted that this is only an indication of difficulty, not the reason for determining the difficulty.
units.reusable_pattern: To make [result] similar to [experience], we define [metric] based on [data]. Note: this is only [indication], not [cause]
reusable_elements: To make [result] similar to [experience], we define [metric] based on [data]. Note: this is only [indication], not [cause]
prohibited_generalizations: Good caveat — distinguish proxy from cause

units.source_excerpt: From a mathematical point of view, the homogeneity and difference of data can be described by distance, and the data can be grouped by distance. Therefore, we decided to use the K-Means algorithm to summarize the difficulty.
units.reusable_pattern: From a mathematical point of view, [property] can be described by [metric], and [data] can be grouped. Therefore, we use [algorithm]
reusable_elements: From a mathematical point of view, [property] can be described by [metric]. Therefore, we use [algorithm]
prohibited_generalizations: Avoid 'From a mathematical point of view' as filler

units.source_excerpt: The above table shows that some attributes have a strong correlation with difficulty. We take the word attributes with greater than 0.6 as the difficulty classification attributes.

reusable_elements: [Table] shows that some attributes have strong correlation. We take attributes with [metric] > [threshold] as [features]
prohibited_generalizations: Justify threshold 0.6 — is it standard or arbitrary?

units.source_excerpt: For the prediction model of the number of reports in Task 1, we fine-tune the intercept of the popularity relaxation function by multiplying it by a certain scale factor to observe the sensitivity of the model.

reusable_elements: For [model] in Task [N], we fine-tune [parameter] by multiplying by [scale] to observe sensitivity

units.source_excerpt: This indicates that the model we have developed is somewhat robust, but is not very applicable to situations where there are large stochastic fluctuations even in steady periods.

reusable_elements: This indicates that [model] is somewhat robust, but not applicable to [edge-case]

units.source_excerpt: We decompose the time series into trend signs and stochastic fluctuations and then make separate predictions. The model built according to this has a good interpretation of the time series patterns.

reusable_elements: Our model relies heavily on [assumption]. However, for [constraint], it is difficult to ensure [assumption]

units.source_excerpt: To mine the Wordle report information, we propose a series of novel models to solve the problem of predicting the number of reports and the distribution of results.

reusable_elements: To mine [information], we propose a series of novel models to solve [problems]

units.source_excerpt: We were happy to dig into the mystery behind Wordle's data through this modeling. Either for the joy of uncovering a puzzle or to spit out a question that is too difficult, the share button allows players to bring their emotions to more people.
